boundedReconciliation.correction: The shown body-tail increment rewrite is sound for its normal-flow example, but not arbitrary bodies with continue. In a for loop, continue routes through update; in the naive while version it bypasses the body-tail update. Preserve that edge, break edge, initialization scope and return edge explicitly.

An invariant is tied to named checkpoints. In a three-clause for loop the end-of-iteration checkpoint follows the update, not merely the last body statement. I and not-guard imply the postcondition only on normal guard-false exit with a pure guard at that state; break/return need separate obligations. With a side-effecting C guard, reason through the guard transition explicitly rather than mixing pre-guard I with post-guard state. Preservation alone does not establish termination.

Nonempty is insufficient for the stated ordinary minimum/equality invariant when NaNs are allowed. For a=[NaN,1], initialized min is NaN and a[loc]==min is false immediately. Restrict to non-NaN inputs or define an explicit total-order/NaN policy. Strict comparison keeps the first minimum among ordinary equal values; the source correctly calls its original tie policy underspecified.

For floating accumulation, an invariant claiming exact mathematical sum requires an exact-arithmetic idealization or a recurrence-defined rounded sum. An integer max-minus-min can exceed int range; its result domain must be explicit. These are added semantic qualifications, not assertions that every source exercise is wrong.

boundedReconciliation.source: Princeton Newton prose and linked Sqrt.java
boundedReconciliation.correction: The blanket claim that each update gets closer in absolute error is false for its initial t=c when0<c<1/9. Independently, c=.01 gives t=.01 with error.09; first update=.505 with error.405. After a positive first step, the estimate lies at/above the true root in exact arithmetic; monotone convergence can then be proved. Machine stagnation/overflow and finite iteration limits remain separate.

Prose describes powers bounded by input n, but linked listing treats n as exponent and prints through2^n. Declare which meaning is used in every authored problem. The listing correctly warns about Java32-bit output limitations. For n=30, its final doubling wraps after the last valid print; translating that update to signed32-bit C17 would still overflow even though its result is no longer printed.

Do not generalize the brief innermost-loop wording to every construct: ordinary break can terminate an enclosing switch; continue targets a loop. Java labelled transfers have no direct C17 break-label syntax equivalent.

The written extern a with omitted type is not valid C17. Rewrite with an explicit type and then resolve identifier binding before predicting output; do not invent a modern result from the historical fragment.

j is not initialized in the shown declaration, so no portable deterministic trace is available. The condition is a comma expression: i<10 is evaluated and discarded; j!=5 supplies the guard. Use initialized bounded int variables in an original problem to isolate sequencing from indeterminate values and char-conversion details.

originalMediumHardDerivations.pattern: Break and continue alter exact checkpoint counts
originalMediumHardDerivations.code: i=0; sum=0; for(;i<8;++i){ if(i%3==1)continue; sum+=i; if(sum>10)break; }
originalMediumHardDerivations.solution: Body indices0,1,2,3,4,5,6. Contributions0,2,3,5,6 give sum16; break leaves i6. Guard evaluated7 times, all true; no final false guard. Update executed6 times, including continue paths at1 and4, but omitted after break at6. A trace must count edges, not append an automatic eighth guard.
States after body processing are12,12,25,37,37. A case0 break leaves switch then adds10; case1 continue bypasses addition but still executes for update. Body5, updates5, guards6, final sum37.

originalMediumHardDerivations.pattern: Postfix false guard versus do-loop first entry
originalMediumHardDerivations.code: Start i=0,count=0 in each independent program: while(i++<4){++count;} versus do{++count;}while(i++<4);
originalMediumHardDerivations.solution: Both guards observe old i values0,1,2,3,4 and finish i5. Pretest body runs4 times; posttest body runs5 times. The failed guard itself increments i. No arithmetic overflow occurs for these bounded values.

originalMediumHardDerivations.contract: n>=0 and all loop increments representable; e.g. n<INT_MAX for signed indices
originalMediumHardDerivations.solution: For outer index i, inner body length n-i+1. Sum_i=1^n(n-i+1)=n(n+1)/2. Inner guards include one false test per outer entry, giving n(n+1)/2+n; outer guards n+1. At n0, inner guards/body zero but outer guard one. Formula products in an implementation require their own range audit.

originalMediumHardDerivations.pattern: Termination by congruence rather than increasing size
originalMediumHardDerivations.code: Unsigned state u starts1 and updates u=(u+6u)&15u; stop on chosen target
originalMediumHardDerivations.solution: The8-state cycle is1,7,13,3,9,15,5,11. Solve1+6t congruent target mod16. Target9 gives6t congruent8, or3t congruent4 mod8, hence t congruent4 mod8 and first hit after4 updates. Target8 gives even left side congruent odd7 and is unreachable. This is a finite-state mathematical reachability proof; do not assert compiled-C execution of a nonobservable endless loop without addressing the C17 optimization permission.

originalMediumHardDerivations.pattern: Useful invariant and a machine-safe variant
originalMediumHardDerivations.contract: Nonnegative bounded integer n with all accumulator values representable
originalMediumHardDerivations.solution: At every guard,0<=i<=n and s=i(i+1)/2. Initialization makes both sides0. Entering with i<n, let old i=k; after update i=k+1 and new s=k(k+1)/2+(k+1)=(k+1)(k+2)/2. Variant n-i decreases exactly1 in the nonnegative integers. Normal exit forces i=n. For n=0 body is skipped. In signed32-bit accumulation, n<=65535 keeps final sum<=2147483647, but computing invariant's product i(i+1) in signed32-bit code may overflow before division; distinguish a mathematical annotation from executable arithmetic.

independentChecks: A separate bounded Python state model checked break/continue trace, switch states, unsigned4-bit cycle and Newton absolute-error counterexample. These corroborate original derivations; they are not C-compiler evidence or a substitute for language semantics.
animationAdvice: Draw initialization, guard, body, update and exit as distinct connected nodes. Continue edges go to the update in for, guard in while and bottom guard in do. Break has its own exit edge.
Animate program counter and state together; show the final failed guard side effect explicitly. A body counter alone cannot explain update or guard counts.
For proof scenes, mark the checkpoint at which the invariant holds, show its temporary disruption and restoration, and use a nonnegative integer variant rather than decorative progress bars.
